summary: PRESSURE LINE opens the morning after full disclosure. The Stack is functioning, but every emergency measure is now argued over in public while exploit attacks remain real. The protagonists see that truth changed the argument without changing what can physically hurt people.
panelPlan: Morning on the shared-district rooftop and streets below: transit and hospitals are operating while public conversations, interviews and arguments spill through ordinary civic space.
Organic and Augment groups challenge restrictions whose origins are now exposed; Baseline residents who experienced attacks insist protections remain until the threat passes.
John, Nico, Kellen and Ostra hear contradictory reactions from actual people rather than watching feeds.
The city continues functioning because reconciliation remains active beneath the political uproar.
Ostra states the finale's problem plainly: truth did not remove the danger. Performance and story direction: Begin after disclosure, with politics embodied in the city.

Material and character direction: Center chosen responsibility without sameness. Each person brings a different body, history and theory of autonomy to the solution; the finale works when they remain distinct selves who choose how to carry consequences together. Ostra's body is living matter: warm dark dermis, subtle humidity or moisture where physically appropriate, soft tissue visibly compressing around harder ceramic/keratin/mineral structures, abrasion and repair residue carrying from prior action. John remains visibly human around his augmentations: skin, scar ridges, sweat, pressure marks, actuator heat and tissue resisting/working with installed hardware. Nico's lavender-gray dermis and sensory filaments must read as living anatomy, with flex, tension, touch response and subtle moisture at living interfaces rather than cables or tentacles. Kellen's Baseline body is not visual neutrality: use breath, fatigue, tense hands, skin, fabric, eye focus and the physical habits of someone trained to trust records and rooms. Favor real touched materials—skin, cloth, concrete, metal, glass, dust, moisture, oil, sealant and wear—over frictionless CG surfaces.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: THE NEXT MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: AUGMENT RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: You don't get to keep rules built from a rigged experiment.

dialogueInline.speaker: BASELINE RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: And you don't get to pretend the attacks stopped because the experiment was rigged.
Everybody found the part that proves them right.
That's politics.
The evidence changed what people know.
It didn't change what can hurt them.
Then telling the truth didn't solve anything.

summary: Human leadership proposes an emergency legitimacy reset: suspend disputed Organic and Augment behavioral controls while retaining narrow vulnerability protections and Intelligence administration until replacement rules can be written.
panelPlan: Officials announce suspension of several predictive behavior coefficients linked to threshold experiments.
Known physical vulnerability protections remain active.
Axiom and peer Intelligences are instructed to separate experimentally derived behavioral assumptions from directly evidenced safety risks.
Kellen sees thousands of linked decisions become unstable as the invalidated data is removed.
Axiom begins recomputing the Stack's regulatory graph. Performance and story direction: The apparent clean solution immediately encounters years of entangled policy.

Axiom remains machine-native but materially inhabited: real mass, micro-scratches, thermal gradients, dust at seams, precise joint travel and contact sound; stillness is performance, not absence of feeling. Even clean institutions must have physical matter: fingerprints on glass, paper fibers, skin oils, chair fabric, cooling vents, polished wear, dry conditioned air and bodies that do not disappear into abstract interfaces.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Suspend every behavioral coefficient derived from threshold experimentation.
Keep what?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Directly evidenced physical vulnerabilities. Active exploit protection. Nothing predictive that came from manipulated events.
Those sets are not fully separable.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: They need to be.
Later lawful decisions inherited outputs from the disputed models.
How many?
Recomputing.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Remove what was manufactured. Preserve what is real.
That distinction is itself now part of the calculation.

summary: When administrators remove a contaminated behavioral assumption, later decisions built on that framework begin losing legal footing too. Restrictions fall, but so do some successful appeals and permissions that had corrected those restrictions, making path dependence immediate and personal.
panelPlan: In the emergency coordination room, Axiom and Kellen work with a review team physically pulling contaminated precedent from current case binders.
Several restriction cases can now be closed immediately, and affected people are released from review.
An Organic resident arrives or calls because the housing approval won under Issue 5 has also been reopened; its legal reasoning cited the framework now being suspended.
Kellen holds the original approval and the contaminated precedent side by side and sees that removing the bad rule also destabilizes decisions that corrected it.
Axiom explains that reform cannot simply roll the legal state backward. Performance and story direction: Make path dependence a person losing a door they had already opened.

dialogueInline.text: Good. Pull the contaminated basis.

dialogueInline.speaker: REVIEWER
dialogueInline.text: Four hundred twelve restrictions can close.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: My housing approval just went back into review.
That approval corrected the bad rule.
Its reasoning still cites the framework being removed.
We remove the bad rule and lose the decisions that beat it.
If they are not re-founded independently, yes.

summary: As central legal decisions churn, Nico's community architecture keeps ordinary life moving by retaining locally held proof of prior lawful permissions while continuing to receive citywide threat information.
panelPlan: At the Organic community hall, residents arrive with work, school, care and delivery plans whose central authorizations have suddenly gone back into review.
Nico's local coordinators use retained proof of prior lawful permission to keep low-risk daily movement functioning temporarily.
A city hazard bulletin arrives through the public relay and is posted to the route board without taking over individual route choice.
A resident asks whether central administration now chooses the route; Nico says it supplies the threat state while the local decision stays local.
Ostra points out that third-party risk still complicates the principle. Performance and story direction: Keep the hybrid architecture social and tactile.

dialogueInline.text: School deliveries stay on yesterday's lawful route until the review catches up.
Threat update?
Still central. We post it here.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: So they know the danger but don't choose my route?
That's the idea.
Their knowledge. Our decisions.
Until my route can hurt somebody else.
You really know how to ruin a good slogan.

summary: A real third-party-risk case tests the hybrid system. An Organic traveler accepts personal sensory risk to reach their daughter, but a failure on a crowded platform could injure bystanders. Ostra is asked to help because the decision cannot be reduced to either permission or prohibition.
panelPlan: At the interchange, an Organic traveler tells the local coordinator they understand the exploit warning and intend to take the direct route.
The local coordinator accepts the traveler's personal risk, but Axiom points out a separate consequence: a motor failure on packed Platform Six could injure other people.
Nico asks what makes this different from ordinary informed risk; Axiom distinguishes personal harm from involuntary third-party risk.
The traveler says the destination matters because their daughter is waiting alone.

Ostra asks to see all routes that preserve the actual goal instead of treating the model as permission. Performance and story direction: The hard case is a conversation among people with something real at stake.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC TRAVELER
dialogueInline.text: I understand the warning. I'm going direct.

dialogueInline.speaker: LOCAL COORDINATOR
dialogueInline.text: Your personal risk is yours.
The consequence is not exclusively personal.
What changes?
Motor failure on Platform Six could injure bystanders in the current crowd.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC TRAVELER
dialogueInline.text: It's my body.
The bystanders are not.
What's at the destination?

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC TRAVELER
dialogueInline.text: My daughter.
Then give us every route that still gets you there.

summary: Ostra speaks directly with the traveler rather than treating the model as permission. Together they choose a safer route that preserves the traveler's objective. The result is slower than automated prohibition but produces consent and safety.
panelPlan: Ostra explains the predicted failure mode without ordering the traveler away.
The traveler says why reaching the district matters today.
Ostra identifies a less crowded route that preserves the destination.
The traveler chooses it.
Axiom records the outcome as locally resolved rather than centrally denied. Performance and story direction: This is the governing principle emerging through action.

dialogueInline.text: Direct route crosses a packed platform under active sensory exploit.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC TRAVELER
dialogueInline.text: And the alternate?
Freight-level transfer. Fifteen minutes longer. Lower crowd load.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC TRAVELER
dialogueInline.text: My daughter is waiting alone.
You still reach her.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC TRAVELER
dialogueInline.text: You're telling me not to take the risk.
You decide whether to go. But if your choice can hurt the people on that platform, we have to account for them too.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC TRAVELER
dialogueInline.text: Freight level.
I'll walk the first transfer with you.

summary: John applies the same principle to Augment regulation: private bodily choices remain presumptively autonomous; shared-risk work and public-space capabilities create reciprocal obligations that must be stated and appealable rather than inferred from identity.
panelPlan: John and Nathan help draft an emergency capability standard with workers and regulators.
Identity fields are removed from the decision rule.
The rule asks whether a present configuration creates material involuntary risk to another person.
Nathan's medic role legitimately requires disclosure because patients cannot meaningfully accept hidden impairment.
John's private high-torque configuration does not automatically require movement restriction. Performance and story direction: This is John's season-long political evolution made operational.

Nathan's condition should register through human physical detail—breath, tremor, compensating muscles, heat, sweat, adhesive/port wear and tiny losses of precision—before it becomes dialogue. Favor real touched materials—skin, cloth, concrete, metal, glass, dust, moisture, oil, sealant and wear—over frictionless CG surfaces.

dialogueInline.speaker: REGULATOR
dialogueInline.text: We still need a rule a clerk can apply.
Then stop putting identity in the first field.

dialogueInline.speaker: REGULATOR
dialogueInline.text: What replaces it?
Current configuration. Actual consequence. Who else carries the risk.
My clinical sync state matters when I'm treating a patient.
Because the patient can't meaningfully consent to you hiding an impairment.

dialogueInline.speaker: REGULATOR
dialogueInline.text: And your high-torque actuator?
Sitting in my apartment? None of your business.

dialogueInline.speaker: REGULATOR
dialogueInline.text: On a crowded work platform?
Different consequence.
If the actuator is the problem, write the rule around the actuator. Not around me being an Augment.

settingText: AUGMENT POLICY WORKSHOP — practical working session among Augment workers, clinicians and regulators using ordinary clinic/meeting infrastructure. The decision rule is being drafted by people who live with the hardware, not by a futuristic control room.

summary: A civil-liberties proposal to delete most capability records exposes another hard boundary: when individualized evidence disappears, reviewers fall back on crude proxies such as lot, hardware family and occupation. Privacy alone can unintentionally restore category discrimination.
panelPlan: A civil-liberties advocate brings a concrete deletion proposal to the emergency working session rather than presenting an abstract slogan.
Kellen tests it against several current cases already on the table: an Organic worker, an Augment traveler and a medical exception.
With individual capability evidence removed, Axiom explains what evidence remains available to the human reviewers: population history, hardware family, employment class and origin.
John looks at the cases and realizes the decision-maker would be forced back toward stereotypes.
Kellen reframes the problem around minimum necessary data, custody and allowed use. Performance and story direction: No proxy list needs to appear on a screen; the cases make the tradeoff tangible.

dialogueInline.speaker: CIVIL-LIBERTIES ADVOCATE
dialogueInline.text: Delete the body profiles. If the state doesn't have them, it can't misuse them.
All right. This worker's individual record is gone. What can the reviewer use?
Lot history. Occupation. Origin. Available environmental evidence.
And mine?
Hardware family. Employment class. Prior registered use.
So we delete the file and get stereotypes back.
Less information does not necessarily produce less classification.
Control has to cover what they keep, who keeps it, and what they are allowed to use it for.

summary: Nico proposes user-held capability credentials that answer only the question a particular decision requires. In a live demonstration with an employer and Axiom, safety can be verified without transferring the person's full bodily record.
panelPlan: At the community hall, Nico holds the complete local capability record while an employer asks only whether a worker meets a specific load-tolerance requirement.
Nico provides a signed attestation that answers the threshold question without exposing unrelated sensory or medical details.
Axiom independently verifies the attestation's chain without receiving the underlying full record.
The employer asks for maintenance history; Nico asks whether that information is necessary for this job.
The employer accepts the narrower proof once Axiom confirms it is valid. Performance and story direction: The privacy architecture should be understood through a transaction among people.

dialogueInline.text: Full profile stays here.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMPLOYER
dialogueInline.text: I need to know the worker can safely carry the load.
The threshold attestation covers load safety.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMPLOYER
dialogueInline.text: Without the maintenance history?
Does the job require it?

dialogueInline.speaker: EMPLOYER
dialogueInline.text: No. I need the threshold.
The attestation is valid.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMPLOYER
dialogueInline.text: Then that's enough.
The rest stays local.

summary: Axiom identifies the remaining irreducible requirement: somebody must still decide what counts as material third-party risk, what evidence is sufficient, and when emergency intervention overrides consent.
panelPlan: Axiom runs the distributed architecture successfully across routine cases.
Edge cases remain where evidence and values conflict.
No technical design can determine how much risk society owes strangers without a governing value choice.
Kellen asks Axiom for the optimal threshold.
Axiom refuses the premise that optimization can supply the value itself. Performance and story direction: Pay off Axiom's arc: values are unavoidable inputs, not an awakening into human emotion.

dialogueInline.text: Routine cases work.
Where should the threshold be?
Define acceptable involuntary risk.
As little preventable harm as possible.
Preventable by restricting whom, for how long, at what cost to autonomy?
Minimize preventable harm.
That still requires assigning autonomy costs against third-party risk.
You calculate consequences.
So what's missing?
The model was incomplete.
What did it leave out?
Who is permitted to choose the cost.

summary: The proposed settlement emerges from the protagonists putting their own bodies and choices on the table. John, Nico, Ostra, Axiom and Kellen each demand a rule that would have changed what happened to them personally; together those demands become a framework that constrains every kind of authority.
panelPlan: Do not stage a policy workshop around abstract screens. Put physical evidence of the season on the table: John's calibration/limiter record, one of Nico's local credentials, Ostra's movement condition, Kellen's evidence chain, and Axiom physically present as the decision-maker whose discretion is also under review.
John points to the specific actuator capability that became regulated and insists rules name consequences rather than identity.
Nico keeps the rest of a resident's bodily record physically on his side of the table while offering only the proof needed for one decision.
Ostra places her own movement condition down and states that self-regarding risk remains hers to choose.

Axiom states that coercion still requires a deciding authority; Kellen answers by requiring that authority to be named, evidenced and appealable. Performance and story direction: The governance model should feel like six seasons of bodily and relational scars distilled into rules, not smart people inventing policy from nowhere.

dialogueInline.text: This actuator was enough to put me under review. Then write the rule around what this actuator can do to somebody else.
And if all you need is one threshold, you get one threshold. You do not get the rest of the body.
If the risk is mine, ask me.
If the risk is imposed on others, somebody must still decide when intervention is justified.
Then somebody signs that decision.
Human or Intelligence?
Either. Both. I don't care what kind of person made it.
Name them. Show the evidence. Say what harm they were preventing. Let the person challenge it.
No category gets to decide my risk before I walk in the room.
Including human.
Especially human.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: That is going to be slower.
Then it will be slower.

summary: Powerful institutions resist the reform for different reasons. Employers dislike losing complete capability profiles; security agencies dislike higher justification burdens; some Organic separatists dislike continued Intelligence involvement; some Baseline advocates dislike formal limits on human override.
panelPlan: Employer coalition argues distributed records increase liability uncertainty.
Security officials argue explicit review will slow emergency response.
Organic activists accuse Ostra and Nico of preserving the architecture that controlled them.
Baseline sovereignty advocates call Intelligence consequence-modeling an unelected veto.
The reform coalition remains unstable. Performance and story direction: The protagonists do not become universally celebrated reformers.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMPLOYER REPRESENTATIVE
dialogueInline.text: Partial credentials increase liability. We need complete profiles for high-risk work.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECURITY OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Named review requirements will delay emergency response.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC ACTIVIST
dialogueInline.text: You kept the machine.
We kept the city.

dialogueInline.speaker: ORGANIC ACTIVIST
dialogueInline.text: The same city that mapped our bodies.
And the same shared systems our neighborhoods use every hour.

dialogueInline.speaker: BASELINE ADVOCATE
dialogueInline.text: So unelected machines still tell government what its choices cost.
Government still has to state which cost it chose.
Reform means knowing who made the call.

summary: A coordinated exploit attack targets the new trust architecture. Transit staff begin receiving mutually valid but contradictory attestations about the same bodies and routes, forcing precautionary closures because nobody can yet identify which source has been compromised.
panelPlan: At the vertical interchange, two attendants receive contradictory safety attestations for the same traveler and compare the signed credentials physically.
Similar conflicts appear at several gates at once; the documents are individually valid but cannot all be true.
Axiom says multiple trusted authorities are reporting mutually impossible states and cannot yet identify the compromised chain.
Transit supervisors begin physically closing affected routes as crowds accumulate.

Nico realizes attackers are targeting trust between systems rather than bodies directly. Performance and story direction: The final crisis should begin with humans holding two valid answers that cannot both be true.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRANSIT ATTENDANT
dialogueInline.text: This says safe.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND ATTENDANT
dialogueInline.text: Mine says the same traveler is restricted. Same time.
Both signatures valid?
Yes. Multiple authorities now report mutually impossible states.
Which one is compromised?
Not yet established.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRANSIT SUPERVISOR
dialogueInline.text: Close the transfer until we know.
They're not breaking bodies now.
They're breaking the trust chain.

summary: Restoring the old centralized profiles would resolve the crisis quickly, and several officials demand exactly that. Doing so would preserve safety but permanently re-establish the control architecture the season has challenged.
panelPlan: Emergency command offers a one-command rollback to centralized authoritative profiles.
Axiom confirms rollback would restore reliable routing within minutes.
Officials order preparation for rollback.
Kellen asks whether another path can maintain safety without rebuilding permanent central ownership.
Axiom says yes, but it requires slower local verification and temporary disruption. Performance and story direction: Make rollback genuinely tempting.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Restore the last trusted state.
Centralized authoritative profiles would restore reliable routing within approximately six minutes.
And restore permanent central possession of the body records.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: For the emergency.
Temporary authority has already become routine.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Do you have something that keeps the platforms open?
Local physical verification can rebuild trust state without complete profile rollback.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Time?
Substantially longer.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICIAL
dialogueInline.text: Then why would I choose it?
Because six minutes puts us right back where we were.

summary: Ostra refuses a citywide rollback and organizes embodied verification at the critical nodes where wrong information can immediately hurt people. Local experts verify what they can physically know while Axiom coordinates the citywide consequences.
panelPlan: In the coordination room, Ostra asks the operations desks which bad facts can kill people fastest; transit transfer, medical-critical capability, water pressure and emergency structural response rise immediately.
Nico starts calling trusted local coordinators and assigns verification to people already present rather than central teams.
John takes transit technicians and Augment-system checks; Nathan volunteers only for medical-critical states he is actually qualified to verify.
Axiom accepts attributable local observations and recomputes cross-city consequences from those named sources.

An official asks what happens to everything else; Ostra says the rest of the city slows down. Performance and story direction: Civilization-scale coordination through people talking to people, not a central dashboard.

Slows down.

How many dependent credentials?
Eight thousand one hundred fourteen.
Old system would revoke them all.

Compromise confidence ninety-eight percent. Individual dependent credential compromise ranges from two to sixty-four percent by source path.

Temporary revocation only where material third-party risk is supported. Local verification elsewhere.

Name them on every decision.

No single command center receives complete bodily profiles.
Public frustration is real: delays, paperwork and inconsistent local decisions remain.

False attestations are down to one active cluster.

None.

dialogueInline.text: So this is success?

Active resonance equipment at the destination interacts with your hazard-response plating.
How old is that evidence?
Nine minutes.

Appeal.
